title: Octopart vs Cofactr
summary: Octopart finds parts and pricing. Cofactr executes the purchase - approvals, POs, supplier tracking, receiving, kitting, delivery to your build.
body_markdown:
##


We all love[Octopart](https://octopart.com/) . It is a go-to place to search for electronic components, find distributor inventory, and compare pricing. But Octopart does not know which suppliers are approved, which offer is best for your requirements, whether the purchase is authorized, how the order should be transmitted, or when it will arrive. Cofactr takes over at that point, turning a part search into an approved purchase and tracking it through delivery.


The two products address adjacent stages of the electronics sourcing workflow. Octopart produces sourcing options.[Cofactr](https://www.cofactr.com/) applies your organization's rules to those options, executes the purchase, and manages the material through fulfillment and delivery.


## At a glance: Part search vs. procurement execution


Part search gives you enough information to make a sourcing decision. Procurement execution turns that decision into conforming material that is ordered, received, recorded, and available for production.


## At a glance: Octopart vs. Cofactr


## What Octopart knows


Octopart is very good at answering the questions that come up before you commit to a purchase. You can enter a manufacturer part number, search a functional description, or upload a BOM and review the component data and publicly reported offers associated with each line.


That information commonly includes:


- Matching manufacturer part numbers and suggested alternates
- Distributors listing the part
- Reported inventory
- Published pricing and quantity breaks
- Manufacturer lead times
- Lifecycle and compliance information
- Technical specifications and datasheets


Octopart's BOM tools can also help match messy line items, compare preferred distributors, examine alternatives, and prepare distributor carts. That beats opening a dozen distributor tabs and trying to recall which one had the full reel, which one had cut tape, and which one changed its inventory count during lunch.


The result is technical and market intelligence that helps you identify a viable part and review the offers available at that moment. It gives you candidate answers to "What can I buy, and where can I buy it?"


Octopart supplies the information needed to evaluate the market. Your internal purchasing process still has to determine whether an offer is acceptable and executable.

## What Cofactr knows


Cofactr organizes your procurement data and purchasing controls. That includes approved suppliers, supplier restrictions, custom pricing, approval thresholds, shipping preferences, delivery targets, and compliance requirements.


Within Cofactr, teams can upload a BOM, evaluate sourcing options, obtain and manage quotes, approve a purchase, track supplier orders, receive material, store inventory, prepare kits, and deliver those kits to production.


By combining Octopart component data with robust controls, Cofactr becomes a true procurement execution platform capable of answering operational questions:


- Which offers comply with your supplier and manufacturer approvals?
- Which purchasing and authorization rules apply?
- Does the offer meet your packaging, traceability, and delivery requirements?
- Has the order received the necessary approval?
- Has the supplier confirmed the PO?
- Has the promised date or quantity changed?
- Has the material shipped, arrived, or entered inventory?
- Is the stock available, allocated, quarantined, packed, or delivered?


Order approvals can be configured around spending thresholds and assigned user permissions. Cofactr also records supplier-order stages such as processing, sent, confirmed, shipped, and received, along with inventory and kit statuses.


True procurement execution converts a collection of distributor offers into a controlled procurement plan.


## Why the lowest unit price can produce a higher total cost


Unit price is seductive because it sits in a neat column and looks easy to compare. Electronics purchasing has a habit of making that neat column rather misleading.


Suppose you need 900 components. Supplier A offers $0.90 each with an MOQ of 2,500 pieces, producing a material cost of $2,250. Supplier B offers $1.10 each and allows you to buy exactly 900, producing a material cost of $990. Supplier A wins the unit-price contest and loses the actual-money contest by a wide margin.


Several commercial details can change the result:


- An MOQ may force you to buy far more than the build requires.
- A lower price break may require enough excess material to increase total spending.
- Order multiples may round the quantity to a full reel, tray, tube, or package increment.
- Freight, tariffs, taxes, brokerage, payment fees, and transaction costs add to the invoice.
- Splitting a BOM across many suppliers creates extra freight and receiving work.
- Consolidating purchases may reduce total cost even when one supplier's unit price is higher.
- Payment terms affect cash flow and the economics of the order.


The same issue appears when you compare offers across an entire BOM. Selecting the lowest line-item price can scatter a purchase among six suppliers, producing six shipping charges, six acknowledgments, six packing slips, and six opportunities for something strange to appear at receiving. A slightly higher component price from fewer suppliers may cost less once the whole transaction reaches your dock.


Landed cost captures the expenses incurred in getting a component ready for production, including transportation, duties, inspection, and material preparation. Cofactr's current cost model also accounts for MOQ and order-multiple rounding, shipping, payment fees, tariffs, customs brokerage, custom reeling, and minimum-order shortfalls.


## How Cofactr finds the lowest total cost


Cofactr evaluates offers using the quantity you can actually purchase and the requirements the supplier must actually meet. Its process accounts for:


- Negotiated pricing from distributors and manufacturers
- Supplier-specific MOQs and order multiples
- The extended cost at each relevant price break
- The quantity required for the current demand
- Forecasted demand that may justify a larger purchase
- Freight, tariffs, taxes, brokerage, and transaction charges
- The added cost of splitting demand among suppliers
- Opportunities to consolidate orders and reduce shipping or handling
- Payment terms and other commercial considerations
- Supplier approvals, delivery targets, end-use restrictions, and purchasing rules


The platform filters offers according to organizational purchasing rules before comparing eligible options. It can account for allowed, preferred, restricted, and last-resort suppliers, along with custom quoted pricing and lead-time requirements.


Cofactr also evaluates the cost of meeting a schedule. An in-stock offer, a three-week backorder, and a six-week factory lead time may have different prices, shipping methods, and production consequences. The useful recommendation is the lowest-cost executable plan that covers the required quantity by an acceptable date.


That distinction matters because a search result records what a supplier reports. Procurement execution follows what happens after you commit money: approval, PO transmission, supplier acknowledgment, shipment, receipt, inspection, inventory, and delivery to manufacturing.

## Where Octopart ends and Cofactr begins


Octopart remains an excellent resource for engineers and buyers who need component specifications, lifecycle information, public inventory, distributor pricing, and possible alternates. It helps you understand the available parts and offers before a purchase commitment is made.


Cofactr carries that information into procurement execution. It applies supplier approvals, negotiated pricing, purchasing authority, packaging requirements, traceability rules, and production dates. It then manages the order through supplier confirmation, fulfillment, receiving, inventory, kitting, and delivery.


The products can work together because they solve different parts of the same workflow. Octopart helps you research the market. Cofactr helps you convert an approved sourcing decision into material that is ready for your build. Finding the part begins the purchasing process; disciplined execution gets it to the production line.

## Frequently Asked Questions


**What is the difference between Octopart and Cofactr?**


Octopart helps users find electronic components, compare distributor inventory, and review pricing. Cofactr manages procurement by applying purchasing rules, creating purchase orders, tracking deliveries, and coordinating fulfillment.


**What information can Octopart provide?**


Octopart provides manufacturer part numbers, alternate components, distributor inventory, published pricing, lead times, lifecycle status, compliance information, technical specifications, datasheets, and BOM matching tools.


**Why isn't part search enough to complete a purchase?**


Part search identifies available sourcing options, but it does not verify approved suppliers, purchasing authority, negotiated pricing, traceability requirements, supplier confirmations, or delivery schedules needed for procurement.


**How does Cofactr improve the purchasing process?**


Cofactr applies supplier approvals, purchasing policies, negotiated pricing, delivery requirements, and internal workflows to create purchase orders, monitor supplier responses, and manage inventory through fulfillment.


**Why doesn't the lowest component price always produce the lowest total cost?**


Minimum order quantities, shipping costs, tariffs, payment fees, packaging requirements, and supplier consolidation can increase overall purchasing costs, making a higher unit price less expensive in practice.


**How does Cofactr calculate the lowest total procurement cost?**


Cofactr evaluates supplier pricing alongside order multiples, negotiated contracts, freight, tariffs, payment terms, delivery dates, and purchasing rules to recommend the lowest executable total cost.


**Can Octopart and Cofactr be used together?**


Yes. Octopart supports component research and market analysis before purchasing, while Cofactr manages procurement, supplier coordination, receiving, inventory, kitting, and delivery after sourcing decisions are made.


**Who benefits most from using Cofactr?**


Companies that purchase electronic components across multiple suppliers benefit from centralized procurement, purchasing controls, inventory management, fulfillment tracking, and logistics that extend beyond component search capabilities.
